title: Number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell
summary: We prove Shi's conjecture that the number of left cells in the second lowest two-sided cell of the affine Weyl group attached to a simply connected simple complex group $G$ is exactly $|W_0|/2$, where $W_0$ is the corresponding finite Weyl group. The same formula holds for the corresponding extended affine Weyl group. The key step is to show that the reductive centralizer in $G$ of a minimal nilpotent element has identity component with simply connected derived subgroup and admits no nontrivial algebraic central extensions by $\mathbb G_m$. This gives an isomorphism of based rings between the asymptotic ring of the extended cell and a matrix ring over the representation ring of the centralizer, with matrix size equal to the Euler characteristic of the Springer fiber, namely $|W_0|/2$.

title: On Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges of compact adjoint orbits
summary: We settle Tam's star-shapedness conjecture for numerical ranges associated with compact adjoint orbits of complex reductive Lie algebras, including its original formulation in terms of the inner product $B_θ$. Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra, and let $K$ be a connected compact Lie group whose Lie algebra is a compact real form of $\mathfrak{g}$. For any $x\in\mathfrak{g}$ and any complex linear functional $f\in\mathfrak{g}^*$, we prove that $\{ f( \operatorname{Ad} (k) x): k \in K \}$ is star-shaped about zero. In the reductive case, the star center is given by the value of $f$ on the central component of $x$, which coincides with the $B_θ$-pairing of the central components in Tam's original formulation. Our proof is uniform for all complex semisimple Lie algebras. Indeed, using the adjoint Casimir operator, we show that all coordinate functions of the orbit map share a common Laplace eigenvalue; we then use a nodal-hypersurface argument to prove star-shapedness for complex-valued functions in a single eigenspace. The geometric argument relies on a two-sided hypersurface-separation property, which holds whenever the first real cohomology group vanishes. In particular, we do not need simple connectivity or real analyticity. More generally, for finite-dimensional representations of compact connected semisimple Lie groups, we establish star-shapedness whenever the nonfixed component of the orbit vector belongs to a single positive Casimir eigenspace.

title: Symplectic singularity as hyperKähler cone
comment: 42 pages. cf., Acknowledgements and use of AI
summary: We prove that any symplectic singularity has a structure of hyperKähler cone. In particular, it is equivalent to the vertex of a conical symplectic variety, and it is automatically K-polystable.

title: Geometry of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra
summary: We give a geometric description of the formal local data of holonomic modules over the first Weyl algebra, the algebra of differential operators in one variable. The exponential part of the associated formal meromorphic connection is encoded by a truncated jet of an affine plane curve at infinity, and the regular part by a regular formal meromorphic connection. We prove that these geometric data uniquely determine the `elementary' blocks in the formal decomposition of holonomic modules. The resulting correspondence is equivariant under automorphisms of the first Weyl algebra, including the Fourier transform.

title: Unique direct-sum decompositions of infinite-dimensional unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group via real CMV matrices
summary:
Unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group arise naturally and play an important role in a wide range of areas including mathematics, physics, and engineering. CMV matrices, introduced by Cantero, Moral, and Velázquez, are five-diagonal unitary matrices that are standard tools in the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle. It is known that every unitary representation of the infinite dihedral group on a separable Hilbert space admits a discrete direct-sum decomposition into representations arising from the natural factorizations of real CMV matrices and copies of two exceptional one-dimensional irreducible representations.
  We prove that such a decomposition is unique up to unitary equivalence when the summands arising from real CMV matrices are grouped according to their multiplicities and the spectral measures of the corresponding matrices are mutually singular across distinct multiplicities. Furthermore, we show that the representation associated with each such real CMV matrix $C$ admits a direct integral decomposition into irreducible unitary representations with respect to the push-forward of the restriction of the spectral measure of $C$ to the closed upper half circle.
  These results make it possible to study the structure of unitary representations of the infinite dihedral group using CMV matrices and the theory of orthogonal polynomials on the unit circle.

title: A cohomology operation encoding the octahedral axiom
summary: We introduce a new secondary cohomology operation, the naturality defect product, associated with a graded natural transformation between the cohomology functors of two differential graded functors, and study its main properties. We then prove that a pretriangulated category satisfies the octahedral axiom if and only if the naturality defect product associated with the natural isomorphism given by a theorem of Heller vanishes on the homotopy category of acyclic complexes over it. This characterization extends immediately to n-angulated categories. As an application, we exhibit non-vanishing instances for the recently found examples of pretriangulated categories which are not triangulated. Finally, we show that horizontal composition of these natural isomorphisms preserves n-angulated structures, and we use it to obtain, from each of these examples and for every r >= 1, a pre-3r-angulated category which is not 3r-angulated.

title: Structural taxonomy and complex irreducible representations of non-abelian groups of order p^4
summary: Let $p$ be an odd prime and let $G$ be a non-abelian group of order $p^4$. The classification of groups of order $p^4$ provides a natural setting for studying the structure of their complex group algebras. In this paper, we consider a non-abelian group G of order $p^4$ and determine the primitive central idempotents of the complex group algebra $\mathbb{C}G$. Using these idempotents, we obtain the corresponding decomposition of $\mathbb{C}G$ into simple components and describe the irreducible representations of $G$. The results provide an explicit description of the representation-theoretic structure of the chosen non-abelian group of order $p^4$ and illustrate the role of primitive central idempotents in the Wedderburn decomposition of its complex group algebra.

title: The modular characters of $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$
summary: Using computational methods, we determine the irreducible $3$- and $5$-modular characters of the symplectic group $\text{Sp}_{10}(2)$ for blocks with non cyclic defect groups, with one ambiguity in the principal $3$-block.

title: Convex orders in root systems and quantum tangent spaces
summary: We classify the reduced decompositions of the longest element $w_0$ of the Weyl group of a semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ for which the corresponding Lusztig quantum root vectors span a quantum tangent space in $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$. We introduce a combinatorial condition on the convex order induced by a reduced decomposition, tangency, and prove that a reduced decomposition gives rise to a quantum tangent space if and only if it is tangent. The proof relies on a description of the coproduct of quantum root vectors in terms of the convex order, and on a projection in the right weak order attached to each positive root. Up to commutation, tangent reduced decompositions are obtained by concatenating the longest minimal coset representatives along a chain of cominuscule parabolic quotients; in particular there are none in types $E_8$, $F_4$ and $G_2$.

title: On characters of irreducible modules for Lie superalgebra q(n)
summary: Su and Zhang proved a formula for the decomposition of characters of irreducible finite dimensional modules over Lie superalgebra $\frak q(n)$ as the sum of Euler characters. They gave a combinatorial formula for the coefficients in that decomposition by generalasing of weights and caps diagrams introduced by J. Brundan and C. Ctroppel. In the present paper we give a correct version of their combinatorial formula. Our main technical tool is a family of creation operators.

title: Exponentially large mu-coefficients
summary: Using webs, we prove that Kazhdan-Lusztig mu-coefficients for symmetric groups grow at least exponentially with the rank, already for pairs labeled by a three-row rectangle.

title: Faithful Localization of Vertex Algebra Modules
summary: We establish a Faithfulness Theorem for vertex algebra modules, showing that two complementary geometric localizations can jointly detect global algebraic structure. We apply this principle to vertex algebras obtained by BRST reduction from classical invariant theory and identify them, under natural geometric hypotheses, with global sections of sheaves of chiral differential operators. As consequences, we prove vanishing of BRST cohomology in nonzero degrees and simplicity, and show that every finitely strongly generated module is a finite direct sum of copies of the vacuum module. In particular, the corresponding module category is equivalent to the category of finite-dimensional vector spaces. For families associated with classical groups, we identify the associated varieties with Hamiltonian reductions, proving quasi-lisse-ness and the predicted identification with Higgs branches of the corresponding supersymmetric gauge theories. This provides geometric realizations of a broad class of vertex algebras arising from three- and four-dimensional quantum field theories.

title: Resolution quivers and the QF-1 property of higher Auslander Nakayama algebras
summary: We give a resolution-quiver-theoretic proof of the QF-1 conjecture of Cruz and Marczinzik for higher Auslander Nakayama algebras of positive even global dimension. The proof combines syzygy calculations in Kupisch coordinates, which show that the projective dimensions of quotients of a fixed projective module with cyclic top strictly decrease as their lengths increase, with a torsion-pair argument and Morita's criterion.

title: Stability functions inducing stability data
summary: In this paper, we study when a stability data on an abelian length category is induced by a stability function. We give an intrinsic characterization of such stability data. For at most six phases, an inducing function exists if and only if every semistable subcategory is wide. An example with seven phases shows that this bound is sharp. For finite phase sets and finite rank, an inducing function exists if and only if an inducing red path exists. We also give a maximal green sequence of length eleven in type $D_4$ that no stability function induces. This disproves the red-path conjecture of Brüstle--Smith--Treffinger.

title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
summary: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

title: Lifting $τ$-exceptional sequences
summary: We study the behaviour of $τ$-exceptional sequences under passage from a finite-dimensional algebra $Λ$ to a factor algebra $Λ/I$. Assuming that $Λ$ is $τ$-tilting finite and that $I\subseteq \operatorname{rad}Λ$, we construct, for every $r$ less than or equal to the number of simple $Λ$-modules, an injective map from the $τ$-exceptional sequences of length $r$ over $Λ/I$ to those over $Λ$. The construction is recursive and is based on lifting indecomposable $τ$-rigid modules and comparing their associated $τ$-perpendicular categories. At each stage, we construct a right exact functor between the relevant $τ$-perpendicular categories which, after identifying them with module categories, is naturally isomorphic to extension of scalars along a quotient $Γ\toΓ/J$, where $J\subseteq \operatorname{rad}Γ$. These functors send each lifted term to an object in the additive closure of the corresponding original term. Finally, we conjecture connections with known bijections for representations of quivers over local algebras and for Nakayama algebras.

title: On derived equivalences of exact structures on the category of representations $k[x]/(x^n)$
summary: From the perspective of homological algebra, exact categories are interesting because they possess derived categories. Typically, an additive category admits many exact structures. If the original category is sufficiently nice (for example, quasi-abelian), a classification of exact structures can be given in terms of certain Serre subcategories in the category of contravariant functors. It turns out that the derived categories of different exact structures are functorially related. This work is concerned with sufficient conditions for the derived equivalence of different exact structures on certain categories.

title: Automatic cocommutativity for the quantum-group comonad
summary:
We prove that the cofree Hopf algebra on a cocommutative bialgebra is again cocommutative, and in fact coincides with the latter's largest Hopf subalgebra. This answers a question of Ardizzoni-Menini-Saracco and provides a proof for a statement to the same effect in the literature, whose original justification contains an apparent gap. The result relies on (and is in fact equivalent to) the observation that cocommutative bialgebra quotients of arbitrary Hopf algebras are automatically Hopf. This latter statement strengthens the analogue due to Newman, which assumes cocommutativity for the Hopf domain.
  One application of the above is the following quantum-rigidity result for Hopf algebras acted upon by a covariant quantum group: an action by one Hopf algebra on another which preserves the unital-algebra structure and the comultiplication factors through an action by a cocommutative Hopf algebra which moreover preserves the entire Hopf structure.

title: A geometric construction of supercuspidal representations
summary: We extend the framework of deep level Deligne-Lusztig varieties to the case of arbitrary residue characteristics $p > 0$. As an application, we provide a construction of a large class of (new) supercuspidal representations for unramified $p$-adic groups with arbitrary residue fields, in a purely geometric way.

title: A nonstandard selfinjective algebra of Euclidean type
summary: Let $\Bbbk$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from $2$. We realize the four-dimensional selfinjective algebra $Ω(1)$ as an admissible infinite cyclic orbit algebra of the repetitive Kronecker category. Thus an algebra long stated to be nonstandard is of Euclidean type in the orbit-algebra sense. We also identify a gap in an earlier proof of its nonstandardness and give an independent proof by determining all connected Galois covering sources of $Ω(1)$. Together, these results disprove the implication from Euclidean type to standardness in the equivalence explicitly stated by Bocian--Holm--Skowroński (2004) and Bocian--Skowroński (2005). They also contradict the standardness conclusion of the Proposition in \S2.1 of Skowroński (1989); its main theorem in \S1.5 assumes standardness and is not contradicted by this example.

title: On the elliptic Hall category
summary: In this paper we study (the positive half of) the elliptic Hall category, a categorical version of the elliptic Hall algebra. Our main result is a computation of categorical versions of the generators in the coherent realization of the elliptic Hall category, i.e., via coherent sheaves on commuting stacks for $\operatorname{GL}_n\times \mathfrak{gl}_n$: we realize them as Hodge associated graded sheaves of certain twisted equivariant $D$-modules on the groups $\operatorname{GL}_n$.

title: Matrix representations of ${\rm BC}_n$ associative Yang--Baxter equations and related long-range spin chains
summary: We construct a matrix representation of the algebra defined by the associative Yang--Baxter equations of ${\rm BC}_n$ type. In the elliptic case, two sets of generators are represented in terms of the Baxter--Belavin quantum $R$-matrix in the fundamental representation of ${\rm GL}_N$, while the remaining generators are represented by the elliptic $K$-matrix found by Komori and Hikami. We revisit its derivation using the Felder--Pasquier procedure and correct the unitarity relation for odd $N$. We then use these matrix representations to construct examples of long-range quantum spin chains from $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for the classical Calogero--Inozemtsev system associated with the ${\rm BC}_n$ root system. We also construct $R$-matrix-valued Lax pairs for Calogero--Moser models in an external field, leading to Haldane--Shastry and Polychronakos--Frahm chains with modified spin positions.

title: On Reed-Muller-Type Codes Associated to Proto-Exact Categories
summary: In this paper, we show how to associate a family of binary linear block codes to the class of admissibly cofinitary objects in any proto-exact category with rank function. This family naturally generalizes the well-studied family of binary Reed-Muller codes, and recovers this classical family for suitable choices of category. We also expand the list of known examples of proto-abelian categories to include incidence categories of posets. As an application of this result, we construct a binormal, combinatorial, proto-abelian category of Kashiwara crystals associated to any root system. In the case that the proto-exact category is a category of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers, we show how to reconstruct our family via the language of algebraic geometry codes, in particular motivating an extension to arbitrary finite fields. We provide explicit computations of the dimension and minimum distance for select families of $\mathbb{F}_1$-representations of quivers.

title: Relative delooping levels on intervals of torsion classes
summary: Let $U$ be a support $τ$-tilting module over a finite-dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq\operatorname{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The exact heart $\mathcal{H}=\operatorname{Fac}U\cap\mathcal{V}^{\perp}$ has an Ext-progenerator $P$. We prove that $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,-)$ realizes $\mathcal{H}$ as a submodule-closed exact subcategory of $\operatorname{mod}B$, where $B=\text{End}_A(P)$, and preserves minimal syzygies. The global relative $k$-delooping levels are independent of $k\geq1$. Writing $g=\operatorname{glo}\text{-}\operatorname{dell}\mathcal{H}$, we obtain the sharp comparison $g\leq\operatorname{glo}\text{-}\operatorname{dell}B\leq g+1$ and $\operatorname{findim}B^{\mathrm{op}}\leq g+1$. Thus the two global levels are finite simultaneously. For wide hearts the relative levels equal their classical counterparts. We also characterize syzygy finiteness of $B$ by a finite relative syzygy stratum and obtain explicit bounds for both finitistic dimensions. If the heart is Frobenius, it is exactly the category of finitely generated Gorenstein-projective $B$-modules under this realization, and both self-injective dimensions of $B$ are at most one. We also give examples to show the main results.

title: Representation type of contraction algebras
summary: We classify the representation-finite, tame, and wild contraction algebras arising from 3-fold flopping contractions of isolated cDV singularities with at worst Gorenstein terminal sources. To achieve this, we first determine the representation type of all contracted preprojective algebras of Dynkin types $\mathsf{A}$, $\mathsf{D}$, and $\mathsf{E}$, and then use the representation type invariance under iterated flops and the radical structure of contraction algebras.

title: Counterexamples to congruences in finite p-groups
summary: Let $K$ be a conjugacy class of a finite $p$-group $G$. Héthelyi, Külshammer and the author asked whether the number of conjugacy classes contained in $KK^{-1}$ is always congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$, and whether, dually, the number of irreducible constituents of $χ\overlineχ$ is congruent to $1$ modulo $p-1$ for every $χ\in\mathrm{Irr}(G)$. We construct a group of order $7^7$ for which both congruences fail.

title: Parabolic filtrations of Soergel bimodules
summary: Given a Coxeter system $(W,S)$ and a subset $I\subset S$. Let $W_I=\langle I\rangle$ be the standard parabolic subgroup of a Coxeter group $W$, and ${}^IW$ be the set of representatives of minimal length in the coset $W_I\backslash W$. We construct a parabolic version of Soergel's standard filtration, and show that, given any Soergel bimodule, each subquotient of its parabolic filtration is a direct sum of grading shifts of $B_x^I\otimes_R R_y$ with $x\in W_I$ and $y\in {}^IW$. By applying the character theorem of Elias and Williamson, we deduce the positivity of coefficients in the expansion of $C_w$ with respect to the hybrid basis $\{C_xT_y:x\in W_I,y\in {}^IW\}$. This generalizes Grojnowski and Haiman's result to any Coxeter group.

title: Stability of certain elements in the Bernstein center
summary: Let $G$ be a split connected reductive algebraic group over a non-archimedean local field $F$ of characteristic zero. The stable center conjecture asserts that the subspace of stable elements in the Bernstein center of $G(F)$ is a sub-algebra, and this subring is conjecturally isomorphic to the regular functions on the moduli of semi-simple Langlands parameters. Bezrukavnikov-Kazhdan-Varshavsky suggested an approach towards the stable center conjecture by explicitly constructing elements and proving their stability directly without assuming LLC, and proved the stability of the depth-$r$ projectors. Following the idea, the first author and Tsao-Hsien Chen produced a family of elements in the center which are conjecturally stable using Deligne-Lusztig parameters attached to irreducible representations. This paper proves the stability of the projectors corresponding to strongly regular Deligne-Lusztig parameters in depth-zero, and for all the positive depth elements with some restrictions on the residue characteristic.

title: Elmendorf's Theorem for $\infty$-categories
summary: Motivated by Teleman's study of gauged topological quantum field theories, our main result is an analog of Elmendorf's theorem in the setting of simplicial group actions on $\infty$-categories. In particular, we prove that if $G$ is a simplicial group, there is a Quillen equivalence between the homotopy category of $\infty$-categories with $G$-action and the homotopy category of $\infty$-category-valued presheaves on the orbit category of $G$. We also show an analog of Whitehead's theorem in this setting.

title: One ring to rule them all: syzygy maximization for Argyres-Douglas
summary: We propose a uniform construction of affine schemes encoding the Higgs branches and Macdonald indices of the Argyres--Douglas theories $\mathcal{D}_p(ADE)$, with $\gcd(p,h^\vee)=1$. The construction captures conjectural OPE decoupling relations via the Jacobian ring of a single invariant polynomial potential, obtained from a polynomial twisted period of the corresponding Coxeter orbit space. We show that these potentials are ``syzygy-maximizing'' in the first jet schemes and recover the Higgs branches as their reduced critical loci. We obtain closed determinant expressions for the classical types and explicit potentials for $E_6$, $E_7$, and $E_8$. Powers of the nilradical define an intrinsic filtration on the resulting Jacobian rings, from which we compute candidate Macdonald indices with the correct Schur and Hall--Littlewood limits, in the examples studied. Restricting the potentials to Slodowy slices extends the prescription to nilpotently Higgsed theories. We further conjecture that these Jacobian rings are isomorphic to Zhu's $C_2$-algebras of simple affine VOAs at boundary admissible levels and their quantum Drinfeld--Sokolov reductions.

title: Non-Induced Representations in Characteristic Zero
summary: This paper explores the failure of induction from all proper subgroups to generate the full representation ring, measured by a quotient group $Q_k(G)$. We extend existing results for cyclic groups to all finite abelian groups and calculate this quotient for all finite groups over fields of characteristic 0 by reducing to the abelian case. We briefly discuss extensions to positive characteristics via modular representation theory. Finally, we detail our result for certain well-known families of groups.

title: Plabic promotions beyond cluster: quantum cluster structures and the dual canonical basis
comment: 101 pages; Supplementary computational data previously included in the v1 TeX source have been reorganized as ancillary files
summary: Plabic tangles define geometric promotion maps between configurations and, after choosing a lift, between Grassmannians. The main conjecture in \cite{Tangles} is that when the tangle is dominant and solvable the induced algebraic promotion is cluster quasi-homomorphism. This work extends the cluster perspective in two directions. First, we initiate the study of quantum promotions. We conjecture that all promotions defined from dominant solvable tangles are naturally lifted to a \emph{quantum cluster quasi homomorphism}, and prove for all cases in the literature that the were shown to be (classical) cluster quasi-homomorphisms. Secondly, we define the notion of cluster-Lusztig quasi-homomorphisms, which are cluster quasi homomorphisms that take Lustig's dual canonical basis elements to dual canonical basis element, up to a Laurent monomial in frozen variables, with clearing and normalization chosen uniformly on each content component. We prove the unexpected result that the classical and quantum $m$-unary star promotions fall into this category, and conjecture that all promotions coming from dominant solvable tangles share the same property. We then consider promotions via non solvable cores of intersection number higher than one. We use it to study facets of amplituhedron cells, and to show that some of them do not lie in zero loci of dual canonical basis elements, disproving a conjecture by T. Lam \cite{LamGP}.

title: Rational limit of Rains integrals of type $A_n$
summary: We deduce the rational analogue of the elliptic Rains identity of type $A_n$ arXiv:0309252. We also derive reductions of the rational analogue and present the connection of them with well-known integrals in literature.

title: Derived equivalence classification of twisted and generalized multifold extensions of affine type
comment: 43 pages. Appendix A has been revised: the proof of Proposition A.2 now uses a covering theorem for group actions rather than the more general 2-categorical machinery. The main results are unchanged
summary: Let $B$ be a piecewise hereditary algebra of affine type over an algebraically closed field. In this paper we give a derived and stable equivalence classification of twisted multifold extensions of $B$. The types $\widetilde D$ and $\widetilde E$ are already covered by the classification for tree type. We therefore consider the remaining types $\widetilde{A}_{p,q}$. We show that the $n$th power of the Nakayama functor on the full subcategory of a transjective component determines the twist, including its action on morphisms, up to conjugacy in the derived Picard group of a hereditary algebra. Together with the hereditary derived type and the folding number, this gives a complete invariant for derived equivalence, and also for stable triangle equivalence. We then compute these conjugacy classes in the unbalanced, balanced, bypass, and Kronecker cases, keeping the finite rotation data. Finally, by the normalization theorem of Asashiba--Kimura--Nakashima--Yoshiwaki, we obtain the same classification for generalized multifold extensions with nonzero integer jump.

title: The algebraic theory of non-archimedean intertwining periods
comment: AI tools have been used; see the corresponding section for details. In this second version, we have replaced the application to quaternionic symplectic models, as we found a simpler proof of the conjecture it was used to establish. We also recover Dat's results on algebraic intertwining operators as a direct application of our algebraic theory
summary: We develop an algebraic theory of local intertwining periods for symmetric pairs $(G,H,θ)$ over non-archimedean local fields $F$ of characteristic different from $2$, and finite-length representations of Levi subgroups of $G$ with coefficients in an algebraically closed field $R$ of characteristic different from the residual characteristic of $F$. For open orbits this algebraic version is essentially contained in the work of Blanc and Delorme. The theory relies on a crucial new uniqueness result, extending a result of Blanc and Delorme for open periods, which asserts that an admissible intertwining period is the only $H$-equivariant linear form extending the corresponding integral on the space of well-supported sections. In the group case it recovers at once the results of Dat on algebraic intertwining operators. Our algebraic construction does not require the unimodularity hypothesis imposed in the work of Matringe--Offen--Yang. When $R=\mathbb{C}$, we also remove this assumption in the classical non-archimedean analytic setting, and prove convergence of intertwining periods for all symmetric spaces. At the same time we extend the context of the whole theory in the following manner: we allow $F$ to be of positive odd characteristic, we allow twisting characters in the periods, and we allow $H$ to lie between $(\mathbb{G}^θ)^\circ(F)$ and $G^θ$. Finally, in the algebraic setting, we obtain explicit polynomial bounds for the singularities of intertwining periods, and compute them in a concrete case.

title: The solvable degree of a Schur algebra
summary:
The solvable degree
  of a Schur algebra $D$ is the greatest common divisor of
  all integers $n$ such that $D^{n\times n}$ is a direct summand of the rational
  group algebra $\Q G$ for some finite solvable group $G$.
  The main result of this paper gives divisibility conditions on the solvable
  degree depending on the center and the rational primes that divide the
  discriminant of $D$.

title: The Brauer $A(\infty)$ condition and Navarro's conjecture on Brauer characters under coprime actions
summary: In this paper, we prove the Brauer $A(\infty)$ condition for good non-defining primes. Consequently, we show a conjecture of Navarro on coprime actions and Brauer characters for primes larger than 3.

title: Wehrl-type entropy problem for compact connected semisimple Lie groups
comment: 11 pages. Reformulated the proof using minimum uncertainty. Simplified some arguments. Updated the exposition and references
summary: Let $G$ be a compact connected semisimple Lie group, and let $π:G\to U(V_λ)$ be a finite-dimensional irreducible unitary representation associated with the highest weight $λ$. We prove that coherent projectors are the unique minimizers of the Wehrl entropy over all density matrices on $V_λ$. Similar extremal properties hold for power functions in place of the entropy function. The proof uses a second variation at the extremizer by perturbation in directions associated with Killing fields, similar to the strategy of Frank and Lieb used in \cite{FrankLieb}. Then the problem reduces to the uncertainty principle characterizing coherent states. This solves the Wehrl-type entropy problem for arbitrary compact connected semisimple Lie groups.

title: Reducibility of linear representations, free ideals, and Kippenhahn's conjecture
summary: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the characteristic polynomial of matrix tuples and finite dimensional group representations. Among other things, several key concepts are introduced, including the minimal polynomial, algebraic extension, spectral index and multiplicity, and characteristic graph. Notably, this framework leads to a complete resolution of Kippenhahn's conjecture by providing necessary and sufficient conditions for its validity.

title: Polynomiality of Stretched Schubert Structure Constants and Key Coefficients
comment: 17 pages, comments welcome. Lean formalization available on request
summary: We prove that monomial coefficients in affine families of key and Schubert polynomials are eventually polynomial. These results extend to finite products. Using M.~Watanabe's Schubert duality, we deduce that stretched Schubert structure constants are eventually polynomial. This proves a conjecture stated by I.~Pak and Z.~Slonim. We also prove that the positive key expansion of every affine-code family of Schubert polynomials eventually has fixed coefficients and affine indices. The proofs combine Demazure operators and vector partition functions with P.~Magyar's orthodontic formula and the generalized Demazure character theory of V.~Lakshmibai, P.~Littelmann, and P.~Magyar.

title: Twisted Yangians of split types BI, CI, DI and Drinfeld type current relations
comment: 45 pages. v2: proofs corrected and expanded, Prop. 2.6 and Cor. 2.7 replaced by Lemma 2.6, new Lemmas 5.5 and 5.13 (§5 renumbered), coideal remark now Prop. 5.20; main results unchanged
summary: We study twisted Yangians associated with the split symmetric pairs of types BI, CI and DI. We introduce a new presentation of these algebras, which we call the transposed presentation, governed by a twisted reflection equation that interacts naturally with the Gaussian decomposition of the generating matrix. Working entirely within the $R$-matrix presentation, we derive Drinfeld-type current presentations of the special twisted Yangian $SY^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ and of the extended twisted Yangian $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$, in which the Serre relations are stated in a closed current form. Extracting coefficients recovers the Drinfeld presentation of Lu, Wang and Zhang, in the normalisation of Lu. As a consequence, we establish an explicit isomorphism between the $R$-matrix and Drinfeld presentations conjectured by Lu, Wang and Zhang. As a byproduct, we obtain a tensor product decomposition of $X^{\mathrm{tw}}(\mathfrak{g}_N)$ into the twisted Yangian in the Drinfeld presentation and a polynomial ring in countably many central variables. We also obtain Poincaré-Birkhoff-Witt bases in the Drinfeld generators and the coideal coproduct on the low Drinfeld modes at all but the last node.

title: The algebraic K-theory of $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$
comment: Corrected statement and proof of main theorem; results now stated over finite fields. Other minor corrections
summary: We compute via trace methods the higher algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring $k[\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)]$, as well as the related groups $\operatorname{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, $\operatorname{PGL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, and $\operatorname{GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $k$ is a finite field of characteristic $p$ and $q=p^r$. At the core of the computation is the algebraic $K$-theory of the group ring of the Sylow $p$-subgroup, $k[C_p^r]$, which we determine via a theorem of Lück--Reich--Rognes--Varisco on cyclic assembly for topological cyclic homology. In the process, we reprove the cyclic assembly result in the language of Nikolaus--Scholze, analyse assembly for smaller families of subgroups, and develop further tools for computing topological cyclic homology of group rings.

title: Representation theory of the real Gelfand order and real Harish-Chandra modules for $\mathsf{SL}_2(\mathbbm{R})$
summary: In this article we study the principal block of the category of real Harish-Chandra modules for the group $\mathsf{SL}_2(\RR)$ and relate it to the category of finite dimensional modules over the so-called real Gelfand order. We describe several distinguished classes of the corresponding indecomposable representations.

title: On the Face Map of the Admissible Set With Parahoric Level
summary: To each face $\mathcal{F}$ of the coweight polytope $\mathcal{P}_μ$, we associate a subset $\text{Adm}(μ)_{\mathcal{F}}$ of the $μ$-admissible set $\text{Adm}(μ)$, which we refer to as a face of $\text{Adm}(μ)$. This gives rise to a face decomposition of $\text{Adm}(μ)$. As an application, we give a complete description of the fibers of the face map $|Δ|^f$ defined by Pappas-Rapoport and prove that the face map is surjective.

title: Prolongation rigidity of sub-free Lie algebras
comment: A few minor improvements and an acknowledgement added
summary: We prove that if the 0-th Tanaka prolongation $\mathfrak{g}_0=\mathfrak{der}_0(\mathfrak{m})$ of a fundamental graded nilpotent Lie algebra $\mathfrak{m}=\mathfrak{g}_{-s}\oplus\dots\oplus\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$ is irreducible on $\mathfrak{g}_{-1}$, then $\mathfrak{m}$ is prolongation rigid: $\text{pr}_+(\mathfrak{m})=0$. The only exceptions are given by negative gradations of maximal parabolic subalgebras of a simple Lie algebra.

title: Representations of generalized linear Reedy categories and abelian model structures
comment: Certain techinical and typographic issues fixed
summary: We study representations of generalized $k$-linear Reedy categories, extending both the linear Reedy categories of Dalezios and Št'ovíček and $k$-linearizations of generalized Reedy categories of Berger and Moerdijk. We establish homological properties of standard modules and classify irreducible representations in terms of simple modules over the local endomorphism algebras. We give criteria for a decomposition of the representation category into a product of local module categories; under the hypotheses of our non-degeneracy criterion, this decomposition holds if and only if the category is Hom-finite over $k$. Applications include span categories and representations of combinatorial categories. Using Grothendieck bifibrations, we then lift families of complete cotorsion pairs on the local module categories to complete cotorsion pairs on the representation category. Under compatibility assumptions, this also lifts families of (hereditary) Hovey triples and yields abelian model structures, with applications to Gorenstein homological algebra.

title: The $ρ$-Fourier transform
comment: Added references to related work of L.~Lafforgue. Added a proof of compatiblity with the Fourier transform in the special case of matrices. Revised section 6 in view of the recent work of Hsu and Yao https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.28507
summary: Let $G$ be a reductive group over a local field $F$ and let $ρ:{}^LG \to \mathrm{GL}_{V_ρ}(\mathbb{C})$ be a representation of its $L$-group satisfying suitable assumptions. Braverman, Kazhdan and Ngô conjectured that one has a $ρ$-Fourier transform satisfying certain desiderata. We give a uniform construction of the Fourier transform for arbitrary local fields. This complements work of L.~Lafforgue in the non-Archimedean case, and proves a portion of the conjectures of Braverman, Kazhdan and Ngô. Our methods are spectral in nature.

title: Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras and \sss-equation
summary: We develop a bialgebraic framework for Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and coalgebras. Starting from dual triangular pre-Lie bialgebras and weak pseudo-Hessian structures, we construct Nijenhuis operators on pre-Lie algebras and establish the corresponding coalgebraic construction. We introduce Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, characterize them through matched pairs, and identify compatibility conditions linking the two constructions. For triangular structures, we formulate the $S$-Nijenhuis $\mathbb{S}$-equation, give an operator characterization, and obtain constructions using relative Rota-Baxter operators. We also show that balanced Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras give rise to Nijenhuis Lie bialgebras. Finally, we introduce crossed modules and braided Nijenhuis pre-Lie bialgebras, and characterize when compatible algebraic and coalgebraic data assemble into a Nijenhuis pre-Lie biproduct. These results connect Nijenhuis operators with pre-Lie bialgebra structures, Yang-Baxter-type equations, and constructions on representations.

title: Endoscopy for representations of disconnected reductive groups over finite fields
comment: Second version: completely rewritten and tripled in size. The first version used reduction to unipotent representations of endoscopic groups, but it turned out that is not canonical and cannot be generalized to disconnected groups in general
summary:
Let G be the group of rational points of a connected reductive group over a finite field. Based on work of Lusztig and Yun, we make the Jordan decomposition for irreducible G-representations canonical. It comes in the form of an equivalence between the category of G-representations with a fixed semisimple parameter s and a category of essentially unipotent representations of an endoscopic group of G, enriched with an equivariant structure with respect to the component group of the centralizer of s.
  Next we generalize these results, replacing the connected reductive group by a smooth group scheme with reductive neutral component. Again we establish canonical equivalences for both the rational and the geometric series of G-representations, in terms of essentially unipotent representations of endoscopic groups.

title: Equidistribution of integers represented by standard quadratic form under arithmetic constraints
summary: We study the equidistribution of integers of the form $n= x_1^2 + \cdots + x_d^2$ under the arithmetic constraints given by $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$. The first step in addressing this problem is to construct modular forms whose Fourier expansion coefficients correspond to the counting problem over the quadric in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ induced by the standard quadratic form, subject to the aforementioned arithmetic constraints. The weak modular property of these modular forms allows us to use representation theory to identify the congruence subgroup to which our modular forms correspond. We then establish a necessary and sufficient condition for functions on $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^d$ that defines a cusp form. Finally, we conclude that the equidistribution phenomenon occurs locally on $p+1$ orbits for $d \geq 4$.

title: On group rings of the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360 and their modules
comment: We proved that Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 also hold for the character of degree 8 of $A_6$, and corrected some errors. After Theorem 1.1, we added a note that Theorem 1.1 holds for general finite groups using an alternative method
summary: Let $p$ be a prime and $\mathbb{Z}_p$ the ring of $p$-adic integers. Let $G$ denote the simple group of order 168, 504 or 360. In this paper, we study the structure of the $χ$-part of a $\mathbb{Z}_p[\mathrm{Im}(χ)][G]$-module come from ideal class groups, Artin $L$-functions and Iwasawa theory. After this manuscript was posted, it was pointed out to the author that the main theorem holds for an arbitrary finite group and follows directly from the structure theorem for group rings; see the note added after Theorem 1.1.

title: Partial actions of groups on monoidal categories
summary: In this work, we introduce the notion of a partial action of a group on a strict monoidal category. We propose, in the context of Monoidal categories, new constructions analogous to those existing for partial group actions over an algebra such as the globalization, the subalgebra of partial invariants, and the partial smash product.

title: Characters of symmetric groups: sharp bounds on virtual degrees and the Witten zeta function
comment: v4: 50 pages, 13 figures. Asymptotic equivalents of the Witten zeta function were added. v3: 50 pages, 12 figures. More general bounds and an application to random maps were added. v2: 44 pages, 12 figures. We added character bounds in terms of the number of cycles and two applications. v1: 37 pages, 11 figures. Comments welcome!
summary: We prove sharp bounds on the virtual degrees introduced by Larsen and Shalev. This leads to improved bounds on characters of symmetric groups. We then sharpen bounds of Liebeck and Shalev concerning the Witten zeta function. Our main application is a characterization of the fixed-point free conjugacy classes whose associated random walk mixes in 2 steps.

title: From Cherednik algebras to knot homology via cuspidal D-modules
comment: Major revisions. A gap in the previous version is filled in: the conclusion drawn from a K-theoretic identity is replaced by a direct computation of characters via shuffle algebras. Results towards cohomology vanishing of relevant sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points on the plane are also added
summary: We prove a rational generalization of Haiman's master formula, conjectured by Gorsky and Neguţ: the bigraded Frobenius character of the associated graded of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the rational Cherednik algebra at slope $m/n$ can be expressed using the generator of the same slope in the elliptic Hall algebra acting on its polynomial representation. The filtration on $L_{m/n}$ is induced by the Hodge filtration on the cuspidal character $D$-module. As a corollary, we relate the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the torus knot to the sum of hook multiplicity spaces of $L_{m/n}$, proving a conjecture of Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. We further provide a realization of the torus knot homology in terms of explicit coherent sheaves on Hilbert schemes of points in the plane.

title: Rational Cherednik algebras and torus knot Invariants
summary: The HOMFLY polynomial of the $(m,n)$ torus knot $T_{m,n}$ can be extracted from the doubly graded character of the finite-dimensional representation $L_{m/n}$ of the type $A_{n-1}$ rational Cherednik algebra as observed by Gorsky, Oblomkov, Rasmussen and Shende. It is furthermore conjectured that one can obtain the triply-graded Khovanov-Rozansky homology of $T_{m,n}$ by considering a certain filtration on $L_{m/n}$. In this paper, we show that two of the proposed candidates, the algebraic filtration and the inductive filtration, are equal.

title: Radical subgroups of finite reductive groups
summary: Radical subgroups play an important role in both finite group theory and representation theory. This is the first of a series of papers of ours in classifying radical $p$-subgroups of finite reductive groups and in verifying the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for them, contributing to the program of proving the Alperin weight conjecture by verifying its inductive condition for finite simple groups. In this paper we present a uniform method for classifying radical subgroups of finite reductive groups. As applications, we investigate the inductive blockwise Alperin weight condition for classical groups, as well as groups of type $F_4$.

title: Group-Frames for Banach Spaces
summary: In the literature, frames generated by unitary representations of groups (known as group-frames) have been studied only for Hilbert spaces. We conduct the first study of frames for Banach spaces generated by isometrically invertible representations of discrete groups on Banach spaces. These frames are characterized using left-regular and right-regular representations, Gram matrices, and group matrices on classical sequence spaces. A sufficiently large collection of functional-vector pairs using the double commutant of the representation is identified to generate group-frames for Banach spaces. Subsequently, we study Schauder frames generated by time-frequency shift operators on finite-dimensional Banach spaces. We derive the Moyal formula, the fundamental identity of Gabor analysis, the Wexler-Raz criterion, and the Ron-Shen duality in functional form.
